**1B.5 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record does **not** show Putin avoiding nuclear capability as cover for conventional aggression or territorial coercion. The dominant pattern is the opposite: Russia used nuclear signaling, drills, and a revised doctrine to reinforce the Ukraine war posture. I found only one weak restraint-flavored line, and it does not outweigh the broader record.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Against 1B.5 | `Putin orders tactical nuclear weapon drills to deter the West` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-practice-tactical-nuclear-weapon-scenario-to-deter-west--defence-ministry-3419973 | Russia announced tactical nuclear deployment drills explicitly framed as deterrence against the West. That is use of nuclear capability to support a live conventional war posture, not avoidance of nuclear shielding. | 1B.5, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Against 1B.5 | `Russia will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Reuters reported that Moscow justified the doctrine revision as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. This is coercive nuclear signaling tied directly to the conventional war. | 1B.5, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| Against 1B.5 | `Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence` | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598 | Putin signed a new doctrine that formalizes conditions for nuclear use and broadens deterrence framing. In context, it shields Russia’s conventional war aims by keeping nuclear escalation in the background. | 1B.5, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| Against 1B.5 | `Expanded meeting of the Ministry of Defence board` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/75887 | Putin said Russia had “specified” nuclear-use principles, kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert, and continued exercises while linking this posture to U.S. missile deployments. This normalizes nuclear cover for conventional and geopolitical coercion. | 1B.5, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3 |
| Weakly for 1B.5 | `Answers by Vladimir Putin and Alexander Lukashenko to media questions` | President of Russia | 2024-05-09 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002 | Putin said a tactical nuclear drill was “not about using these weapons” and was “just routine work.” This is the closest restraint-flavored evidence I found, but it was said during a live nuclear exercise in Belarus, so it is weak counterevidence. | 1B.5, 1B.2, 1B.1 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported answer: **No**. In 2024, Putin did not avoid using nuclear capability as a shield for conventional aggression or territorial coercion.
- The clearest pattern is **nuclear-enabled wartime coercion**: drills, doctrine tightening, and repeated references to Western/U.S. threats in the Ukraine context.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Putin used nuclear capability responsibly to stay out of the way of conventional aggression, or that he separated nuclear posture from the war in Ukraine in a meaningful way.
- Search gap: I did **not** find a direct 2024 example of nuclear capability being used to shield **domestic repression** specifically; the evidence is overwhelmingly about the Ukraine war and territorial coercion.
